newsitem.title: FRANCE: France studies medical control for sex offenders.
newsitem.headline: France studies medical control for sex offenders.

text.p: Justice Minister Jacques Toubon, questioned on the rape and murder of four young women in northern France, said on Tuesday he was studying the possibility of imposing treatment on jailed sexual offenders.
Toubon reiterated that a bill to be put foward to parliament in April provided for compulsory treatment and care by social services after the offender left jail.

"The mechanism is very simple. A doctor sent by a judge chooses in consultation with the convicted offender, at the time of his release, a doctor who will take care of him. If this obligation is not respected, the offender will return to jail," Toubon told the National Assembly (lower house).
"Some people say the compulsory treatment should start before the prison sentence runs out. I am studying a formula which I will probably submit to parliament," Toubon said.

An autopsy on the four student girls has confirmed that they were beaten and raped before they were murdered and buried in the sand on a beach near Boulogne. Three of the victims carried marks which appeared to show that they had been strangled.
Two scrap-merchant brothers have been detained and placed under investigation on suspicion of rape and murder.

Prosecutor Gerald Lesigne named the suspects as Jean-Louis Jourdain, 37, and his brother Jean-Michel, 34. He said the elder brother was freed in 1995 after serving 11 years of a 15-year prison term for strangling a teenage girl to death. The younger was released in 1994 after serving eight years of a 10-year term for rape.
The killings have prompted calls for the restoration of the death penalty.
Peggy Merlin, 20, and her 17-year-old sister Amelie, Isabelle Lamotte, 20, and her sister Audrey, 17, went missing this month during a carnival evening in Boulogne.

Their bodies, in fancy carnival dresses, were found hastily buried in the sand near a concrete bunker built by German forces during World War Two on a beach outside the village of Dannes, where the suspects live, 10 km (six miles) from Boulogne.
Police said the girls, who disappeared in the early hours of February 12, were apparently killed on the following evening.
